Patrícia, I read the account plan. It is ambitious. Can we really do all this in one fiscal year?
I think so. The kickoff is in January, and by the end of February we will have moved the twelve stores.
And in March? My store managers are very busy in March.
I know. In March our team will be training them in small groups, one hour a week, not more.
Good. What about the go-live of the app? My CEO asks me about it every week.
The app goes live in May. By then, every manager will have received a login, and we will be sending you weekly reports.
And the twenty new stores? That is the part that worries me most.
That is our stretch goal. If the openings are ahead of schedule, we will add a checkpoint in September.
That is our stretch goal, not a promise.
Let's book a checkpoint before your budget review.

Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. I read the Brightwave account plan. It is the best one in the team, and I want to use it as an example. One small suggestion before you send it. In each phase, write one sentence with a date and a result, like: by the end of February, we will have moved twelve stores. Customers remember dates, not activities. Then, for the busy months, say what your team will be doing, so that the customer knows what to expect. And please add the forecast for the twenty new stores, even if it is not certain. A number with a risk is better than no number. Send it to Daniel before the checkpoint on Friday, and copy me.

Hi Patrícia, it is Arjun, about the Brightwave plan. I checked the technical side, and most of it is realistic. By the end of January, we will have finished the tests for the new region, so February is fine for the move. The mobile app is the tight part. In April, my team will be fixing the last bugs, so the go-live in May is possible, but not early. Please do not promise that we will be ahead of schedule there. One more thing: by the time the twenty new stores open, the nightly file will have doubled again. I will be watching the sync closely, and the alert will tell you if anything is slow.
